objective: Record a newly surfaced accepted-paper no-go theorem with exact model-class and measurement-scope boundaries, and define an independent falsifiable reproduction gate without promoting quantum-foundations theory into technology evidence.

sources.title: No-go theorem for maximally ψ-epistemic models using two pure states of a qubit
sources.venue: Physical Review A — APS accepted-paper record
sources.reported_result: Under the stated assumptions, maximally ψ-epistemic models cannot reproduce the relevant non-projective-measurement statistics for a pair of pure single-qubit states; the construction uses a two-input, three-output RAD game and the equal mixture.
sources.limitations: Accepted-paper record, not independently reproduced by UQPU; scoped model class and measurement assumptions; no technology, energy, material, fusion, finance, or new-physical-law result.

required_steps: Freeze accepted-paper version, definitions, state vectors, allowed non-projective measurement, RAD payoff, assumptions, and source hash.
Independently derive the overlap inequality and RAD score bound; prefer exact arithmetic or preregistered interval tolerances.
Test projective and stated non-projective controls, state-label exchange, and mixture-probability perturbations; retain counterexamples.
Compare against an independent implementation and reviewer; optimizer agreement alone is not proof.
If an experiment is justified, preregister calibration, finite-shot confidence intervals, leakage, drift, and a discriminating RAD-score observable.
Keep proof, simulation, and laboratory evidence separate; require matched useful-output/economics contracts for any technology claim.
next_gate.falsifier: Independent derivation or counterexample contradicts the source inequality under its stated assumptions, or a frozen numerical fixture violates the derived bound beyond the declared error budget.
next_gate.acceptance_rule: A reproduced theorem validates only the frozen mathematical statement under explicit assumptions; no automatic promotion to physical law, QPU advantage, or economic result.
